ACTION: Freeze deploys and CI for affected services; block the bad version in the registry proxy/firewall (Artifactory, Nexus, pip/npm config)
Pin to the recommended safe version in manifest + lockfile; regenerate lockfile with --frozen/--require-hashes
Purge package caches (~/.npm, node_modules, pip cache, wheelhouse, Docker layers) and rebuild images from clean base
Treat every host/CI runner that installed the version as compromised: re-image, do not just uninstall
Rotate all secrets reachable from affected hosts, from a clean machine
Hunt IOCs in egress/DNS/auth logs for the install window (from first publish of bad version until pin); check for new persistence files
Check egress to AI/LLM endpoints and anonymizers (Edg3 egress + Tor lists) from affected hosts
Notify downstream consumers in blast radius; file incident record with timeline
Confirm installed version is in affected range and the vulnerable code path is reachable (feature/config used?)
Prioritise: CRITICAL/HIGH, exploited-in-the-wild (CISA KEV / DVE score), internet-facing tier first
Upgrade to the lowest fixed version on the current major; open PR with tests
No fix yet: apply compensating control (WAF rule, header strip, disable feature flag, input limits)
Re-scan lockfile, run test suite, replay sanitized production requests in staging
Human reviews diff, reachability evidence and rollback plan before merge
Package/version unpublished or yanked: pin to last good published version
Serve from internal mirror/vendor directory; enable registry proxy caching
If yanked for security reasons, escalate to MALICIOUS_RELEASE or VULNERABILITY playbook
CA bundle change (e.g. certifi): diff added/removed roots vs current bundle
Upgrade certifi or OS trust store; check services pinning certificates or using custom bundles
Run TLS handshake checks against all outbound dependencies before rollout
